name: Gudskul (ruangrupa / Serrum / Grafis Huru Hara)
funding: Communal resource pool (lumbung), DOEN Foundation, Arts Collaboratory, and cooperative commercial enterprises. Completely non-corporate collective governance.
watch: Ecosystem and educational collective formed by ruangrupa (curators of documenta fifteen), Serrum, and Grafis Huru Hara. Pioneered the 'lumbung' practice of shared resources, collective decision-making, and communal art-making.
records_note: Its site publishes no annual report, accounts, board or funder names; the about page says only that donors, sponsors and its own units pay.

name: Khoj International Artists' Association
funding: Artist-run since 1997. Top supporters: Prince Claus Fund, Goethe-Institut New Delhi and Ford Foundation; capital circle includes Apeejay Trust, Inlaks India Foundation, Weikfield; benefactor Sangeeta Jindal.
watch: Benefactor Sangeeta Jindal (JSW Foundation): JSW is mostly steel; its power arm is about 5% of group revenue (US$1.1B of US$23B).
records_note: No annual report or audited accounts, only foreign-contribution filings from 2012; it names donors by tier, undated, and lists an eight-member board plus advisors.

name: A4 Arts Foundation
funding: Endowed not-for-profit foundation (Wendy Fisher / Kirsh Foundation) and independent institutional partners.
watch: 2018 boycott call over the funder's security holdings.
why_flagged: 2018 boycott call over the funder's security holdings.
records_note: No annual reports, accounts, donor list or board found; the team page lists staff only.

name: LACE (Los Angeles Contemporary Exhibitions)
funding: California Arts Council, Andy Warhol Foundation, National Endowment for the Arts, Mike Kelley Foundation. 501(c)(3) public non-profit returns.
watch: Founded in 1978 by a group of rebellious artists, LACE is the longest-running non-profit artist-run space in Los Angeles. Known for championing experimental performance, social justice dialogue, and video archives.

name: CUE Art Foundation
funding: National Endowment for the Arts (NEA), NYSCA, NYC Department of Cultural Affairs, private philanthropic grants. 501(c)(3) public non-profit.
watch: Dedicated to creating opportunities for emerging and underrepresented artists of all ages.

name: Mercer Union
funding: Canada Council, Ontario Arts Council, Toronto Arts Council. TD Bank Group leads support for a communications post; Burdock Brewery is beverage sponsor.
watch: TD Bank pleaded guilty in October 2024 to money-laundering conspiracy and Bank Secrecy Act failures, paying about $3B.
records_note: Names about 35 donors, three funders and its sponsors, lists an 11-member board and posts its 2024-25 impact report, but no financial statements.

name: Western Front
funding: 2025-26: Canada Council, BC Arts Council, Province of BC and City of Vancouver, with the Audain Foundation and Western Front Foundation at $20k+.
watch: One of Canada's oldest and most revered artist-run centres, founded in 1973 in a historic Knights of Pythias hall. Artist-run centre founded in 1973 by eight artists. Its building was bought in 2015 with C$1.5M of developer Rize's city amenity money.
records_note: Western Front posts annual reports for 2021 to 2026 with audited-statement summaries, a named 2025-26 supporter list and its board.

name: Pivô
funding: Federal Cultural Incentive Law (Lei Rouanet), philanthropic patron circle, international cultural foundations. Independent Brazilian non-profit audit.
watch: Independent cultural platform occupying a monumental 3,500m² space inside Oscar Niemeyer's Copan Building in downtown São Paulo. Dedicated to site-specific commissions, an international research residency (Pivô Pesquisa), and open public debate.

name: L'Appartement 22
funding: Founded by curator Abdellah Karroum. Supported through non-commercial international research grants, Prince Claus Fund, and independent publishing sales.
watch: The first independent space for contemporary visual art and curatorial research in Morocco, founded in 2002. Operates as an open curatorial laboratory, radio station (R22), and residency platform for Maghrebi and African artists.

name: Bag Factory Artists' Studios
funding: National Arts Council South Africa, Triangle Network, international cultural foundations, studio rentals. Registered Non-Profit Organisation (NPO).
watch: Historic non-profit artist-led organisation founded in 1991 during the final years of apartheid by David Koloane, Robert Loder, and Ricky Burnett. Created to provide a safe, non-racial studio space where Black and white artists could work together freely.

name: Spike Island
funding: £1.5M income (FY2025). Arts Council England £285k, Bristol City Council £30k, John James Foundation, Henry Moore Foundation, Pilgrim Trust, Ampersand, Art Fund; Hauser & Wirth partnership to 2028.
watch: Monumental 80,000 sq ft production and exhibition space for contemporary art and design on Bristol's historic harbourside. Houses over 70 artist studios, fabrication workshops, and major non-commercial gallery spaces.
why_flagged: £1.5M income (FY2025). Arts Council England £285k, Bristol City Council £30k, John James Foundation, Henry Moore Foundation, Pilgrim Trust, Ampersand, Art Fund; Hauser & Wirth partnership to 2028.
records_note: Names supporters by tier with no date and lists its trustees; no annual reports posted, accounts for 2021 to 2025 sit on the register.

name: Hangar.org
funding: Generalitat de Catalunya Department of Culture, Ajuntament de Barcelona, European cultural research programs. Non-profit artist association.
watch: Artist-run center for visual arts research and production in Poblenou.
